_comment: User-authored strategy. Nothing in this repo may generate, tune or rank a rule;
the code only evaluates what is written here.
Field paths are dotted paths into the /technicals payload. There is no
field-to-field operator on purpose, so 'close is below the 50-day average' is
written as trend.pct_from.sma50 < 0 - the same statement, as a literal.
'codes' scopes the universe. Leave it empty to consider every US holding and
watchlist name the paper account is authorised to trade.
max_fee_pct_of_notional refuses an entry whose estimated round-trip cost is a
bigger share of the position than this. Fees here are nearly flat ($0.99
platform + ~0.115% stamp duty), so small positions are punished: a $650
position owes 0.55% round trip, a $1,950 one owes 0.35%. At 0.50% the engine
will not take a position under roughly $825.
max_orders_per_day, max_orders_per_symbol_per_day and cooldown_days are all
budgets on NEW exposure - they count and gate entries only. An exit is never
refused by them, because a position the rules want closed must always be
closable. Raising this cap therefore buys more entries, not more churn.
What actually limits entries per day here is max_concurrent_positions (8) and
cooldown_days (1): a slot has to be free before anything new is bought, so a
cap above 8 is an outer safety limit rather than the throughput lever.
max_open_notional_pct is measured against the REAL account's equity, because
that is what sized the position - against the paper account's own million it
would never bind. On ~13k of real equity, positions land near 900-1,500, so 8
of them is roughly 74%: below 80 this ceiling would bind before the position
count did and the 8 would be decorative.
Note that max_notional_pct is rarely the binding constraint on this account:
risk_pct 1% over a 2x ATR stop already caps most positions near $900-1,500,
below the 15% ceiling. If you want the fee burden proportionally smaller, the
lever is a larger position - raise risk_pct or tighten atr_mult_stop - not a
looser limit here. The paper account is charged nothing, so without this
guard the simulation would count fee-driven losses as wins.
